resources.string: No novice/expert permission profiles. No artificial capability gates.
Claiming is exclusive: while the interface is held, no other owner on this host can use it. Nothing is claimed automatically.
Re-examines attached devices and asks for permission again where it is missing.
No device attached. Connect a device over USB.

Protocol mode is unknown until a handshake. Descriptors distinguish an ADB class interface from a Fastboot class one, but not Android from Recovery or Sideload, nor bootloader Fastboot from fastbootd.

A recognised device is connected automatically: the interface is claimed and the ADB handshake runs. The device may ask you to allow debugging from this host. Disconnecting stays in effect until the device is reattached.
Public key sent; waiting for device authorization. Android may show an RSA confirmation dialog.
Unknown peer, banner prefix not recognised
Devices have not been examined yet.
The system reports no USB devices at all. Check OTG, the cable and the adapter: without a device there is nothing to ask permission for.
The system reports %1$d USB device(s), but none of them exposes an ADB or Fastboot interface.
This host reports no USB host mode support, so no device can be examined.
The command runs in a non-interactive shell and ends on its own. Output is capped at 64 KiB and the call has a 30 second deadline.
Exit code is unavailable: the device does not support shell,v2.
Line to send to the shell
Opening shell; waiting for the device to confirm the stream…
Closing shell; waiting for the ADB stream to release…
The shell is open and waiting for input.

The shell stays open until you close it. Single commands and file operations keep working meanwhile — each runs on its own stream. Escape sequences are shown as they arrive; they are not interpreted yet.
Path on the device, for example /sdcard/Download/file.zip

Writing creates the file at that path and overwrites whatever is there. The content is generated by the app: choosing your own file needs the artifact source that comes later. On failure the app says what it knows about the file, and "unknown" means exactly that — check it on the device.
Write failed: %1$s. Nothing was written: the request never left this host, so %2$s is untouched.
Write failed: %1$s. The state of %2$s is unknown: the request had already left this host, and the device may hold a partial file. Check it before retrying.
Write reported failure after the device had confirmed it: %1$s (%2$s). This combination should not occur; please report it.
Reading does not save anything: it checks the transfer. Compare the hash with sha256sum on the device — matching hashes prove the bytes arrived intact. Saving to a place you can reach comes later.
Target: empty for system, bootloader, recovery
Accepted: %1$s — the device is going down

Success looks like a disconnect: the device leaves the bus and the link closes. Targets are not restricted — the device knows which ones exist. UNTOUCHED means the request never left the host and retrying is safe; UNKNOWN means it left without confirmation, so do not retry.
Service name, for example shell:ls or sync:
%1$s — accepted, the device left the bus (%2$s)

The service name is passed through as typed; there is no list, because the device knows which services exist. The response size is always named — a service may not answer with text at all, and then the byte count is the only thing known for certain. A reboot: typed here behaves like the reboot button.
Local port, 0 for any free one
Address on the device, for example tcp:5555

The listener is bound to loopback and reachable only from this phone; there is no way to open it to the network. The address is passed through as typed — which addresses exist is known by the device. One forward carries up to %1$d connections at a time: behind each are two blocking loops, and the limit is about our threads, not about what may be asked for.
